name: Master Thief (Prestige Class)
body:
A master thief is the living embodiment of greed, someone who steals habitually and with impunity. A master thief is clever and crafty, always with an eye out for their next prize and always thinking three steps ahead about the best way to obtain it without getting caught. They may be a cutpurse, a cat burglar, a swindler, or a safe-cracker, but they master the arts of larceny with a skill few can match. Master thieves often acquire a reputation in the criminal underworld and attract minor accomplices and hangers-on looking for a piece of the action with a lord among thieves, and most found their own guilds and set up networks of informants to keep themselves apprised of new opportunities for personal enrichment. Adventuring master thieves look for challenges that exceed those available to them in the back alleys and high society of the cities, finding exotic and amazing treasures to put on display. Master thieves almost always have rogue levels, though many begin their careers in crime as bards, inquisitors, investigators, rangers, and slayers.

Requirements

To qualify to become a master thief, a character must fulfill all the following criteria:

Feats: Improved Steal
Skills: Acrobatics 5 ranks, Appraise 5 ranks, Bluff 5 ranks, Climb 5 ranks, Disable Device 5 ranks, Perception 5 ranks, Sleight of Hand 5 ranks, Stealth 5 ranks
Class Features: Black market connections rogue talent, sneak attack +1d6.
Special: An aspiring master thief must have personally stolen treasures worth at least 1,000 gp without being detected.
Hit Die: d8
Class Skills

The master thief ‘s class skills are Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), Stealth (Dex), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 8 + Int modifier.

Table: Master Thief
Level	Base Attack Bonus	Fort Save	Ref Save	Will Save	Special
1st	+0	+0	+1	+0	Case the joint, smash and grab, thieves’ cant
2nd	+1	+1	+1	+1	Eye for treasure, looter’s bag
3rd	+2	+1	+2	+1	Rob you blind, rogue talent
4th	+3	+1	+2	+1	Light-fingered larceny, quick getaway
5th	+3	+2	+3	+2	Backstab, guarded stash, guildmaster
6th	+4	+2	+3	+2	Rogue talent, safecracker
7th	+5	+2	+4	+2	Elude detection, lucky strike
8th	+6	+3	+4	+3	Den of thieves, uncatchable
9th	+6	+3	+5	+3	Rogue talent, slither away
10th	+7	+5	+3	+3	Greater backstab, supreme stealth
Class Features

The following are class features of the master thief prestige class.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Master thieves are proficient with all simple weapons and martial light weapons, as well as rapiers, shortbows, and whips, and with light armor and bucklers (but not other shields).

Case the Joint (Ex)

A master thief gains the quick scrounge rogue talent, and for each class level they reduce the duration required to search an area by one round (or by one step, if already requiring a full-round action or less). Alternatively, if they spend the time normally required to search an area, they can search a number of creatures or 5-foot-squares equal to their class level as part of the same action. All creatures or areas to be searched must be within 10 feet of the master thief, though this range increases to 20 feet at 5th level and to 30 feet at 10th level.

Smash and Grab (Ex)

A master thief gains Quick Steal as a bonus feat. If they use a standard action to attempt a steal combat maneuver, they add their class level as a bonus on their combat maneuver check.

Thieves’ Cant (Ex)

A master thief adds their class level as a bonus on Bluff checks made to communicate a hidden message and on Sense Motive checks made to intercept a hidden message. A Bluff check to send a hidden message automatically succeeds if the recipient also has levels in this prestige class.

Eye for Treasure (Ex)

At 2nd level, a master thief can use the skill unlocks for Appraise as though they had 5 more ranks in that skill than they actually possess.

Looter’s Bag (Su)

At 2nd level, a master thief can treat any bag, pouch, backpack, pocket, or similar container they carry as a bag of holding (type I).The bag itself does not radiate magic, as if shrouded with a magic aura spell, and any objects stored within it are treated as if were protected by nondetection with a caster level equal to the master thief ‘s character level. At 4th level, they can cause their looter’s bag to duplicate a bag of holding (type II), at 6th level a bag of holding (type III), and at 8th level a bag of holding (type IV), and at 10th level a portable hole. A master thief may have only one looter’s bag at a time. However, at 5th level and above they may choose to split their looter’s bag into three separate containers, equivalent to the three pockets of a handy haversack. These three containers may be located anywhere on their person and need not be part of the same container. If the looter’s bag is separated from the master thief, it loses its magical properties after a number of hours equal to their class level.

Rob You Blind (Ex)

At 3rd level, whenever a master thief makes a successful steal combat maneuver, they can attempt a dirty trick combat maneuver against the same target as a free action. This does not provoke attacks of opportunity. Despite the name, the master thief can use this dirty trick maneuver to inflict conditions other than blindness on the target.

Rogue Talent

At 3rd level and every 3 levels thereafter, a master thief can select a rogue talent for which they qualify, treating their class level as their rogue level. Their master thief levels stack with their rogue levels for the purpose of qualifying for rogue talents and advanced rogue talents and when determining the effect of level-based rogue talents.

Quick Getaway (Ex)

At 4th level, a master thief can use the withdraw action as a move action, moving a distance up to their speed. If they use a full-round action to perform the withdraw action, they can move up to twice their speed, and the number of squares at the beginning of their movement that do not provoke attacks of opportunity are equal to one?half their class level. If the master thief is affected by a fear effect when they use the withdraw action, they gain a dodge bonus to their AC equal to one-half their class level until the beginning of their next turn.

Light-fingered Larceny (Ex)

At 4th level, a master thief gains Greater Steal as a bonus feat and can use the skill unlocks for Sleight of Hand as though they had 5 more ranks in that skill than they actually possess.

Backstab (Ex)

At 5th level, when a master thief adds 1d6 to their sneak attack damage, and their master thief level stacks with their rogue level for the purpose of overcoming improved uncanny dodge. In addition, when they confirm a critical hit against an opponent that is flanked or is denied its Dexterity bonus, their critical modifier is increased by 1.

Guarded Stash (Sp)

At 5th level, whenever an object that a master thief has kept on their person for at least 24 hours is removed from their person, it triggers a silent mental alarm similar to an alarm spell, and once per day they can use locate object as a spell-like ability to locate an object that has been removed. A container they are using as their looter’s bag is warded by a magical effect similar to illusory script, save that the embedded suggestion affect takes effect when a creature attempts to open the container rather than reading the affected item. The save DC of this effect is Charisma-based.

If the master thief has constructed a building, as described in the guildmaster ability, they may designate one room within that building to share the benefits of this ability. That room is warded by a permanent alarm and one container within it with a magical effect akin to illusory script, and they can use their locate object ability to find an object that has been removed from that room.

Guildmaster (Ex)

At 5th level, a master thief gains a +2 circumstance bonus on all Charisma checks and Charisma-based skill checks made with any character that has rogue levels. This bonus increases to +4 at 10th level, and it also applies to the guildmaster’s fame and on skill checks a master thief makes when interacting with contacts. If the master thief has the Leadership skill, a cohort with rogue levels can be within 1 level of the master thief ‘s character level.

If using the downtime rules from Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Ultimate Campaign, a 5th or higher-level master thief can construct a building (often a tavern, though many master thieves choose theaters, guildhalls, luxury stores, or even temples as their “cover” buildings). When they do so, they immediately acquire one reliable contact in the same city or town in which that building is located. Regardless of which type of building they construct, they also attract the service of a thieves’ guild (see the “Buildings and Organizations” section of chapter 2 in Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Ultimate Campaign) at no cost and without needing to take time to build that organization. If this thieves’ guild is destroyed, they can replace it at half the normal cost in capital and time. This thieves’ guild can perform any actions that an organization of its type can normally perform. When rolling d% to determine thieves’ guild events, a master thief may add or subtract their class level from the result of the die roll to determine which event occurs.

Safecracker (Ex)

At 6th level, a master thief can use the skill unlocks for Disable Device as though they had 5 more ranks in that skill than they actually possess.

Elude Detection (Sp)

At 7th level, a master thief can befuddle divinations used against them as if they were under the effect of a nondetection spell with a caster level equal to their character level. They can suppress or resume this protection as a standard action. If dispelled, the master thief cannot resume the nondetection for 1d4 rounds.

Lucky Strike (Ex)

At 7th level, when a master thief misses on an attack against a creature that is flanked or denied its Dexterity bonus, as a swift action they can reroll the attack. They can use this ability once per day, plus one additional time per day per level above 7th.

Den of Thieves (Sp)

At 8th level, once per day a master thief can ward some or all of their personal building with a mage’s private sanctum, with a caster level equal to their character level. They may instead choose to ward only a single room, increasing the duration to a number of days equal to their character level. At 10th level, a master thief can duplicate the effect of screen rather than mage’s private sanctum, affecting some or all of their building for 24 hours, or a single room for a number of days equal to their character level.

Uncatchable (Ex)

At 8th level, a master thief gains a +4 bonus to their CMD against grapple combat maneuvers and on Escape Artist checks. They can also use the skill unlocks for Escape Artist as though they had 5 more ranks in that skill than they actually possess.

Slither Away (Ex)

At 9th level, when a master thief can take a 5-foot step as an immediate action whenever they are attacked by a creature they have damaged with a sneak attack since the beginning of their last turn. If this 5-foot step moves the master thief out of the target’s reach, the attack automatically misses. If the master thief is still within the target’s reach, they gain a +4 dodge bonus to AC against that attack. For determining cover, concealment, line of sight, or line of effect for the attacker, use the worst of the master thief ‘s original location or their new location.

Greater Backstab (Ex)

At 10th level, a master thief ‘s sneak attack damage increases by an additional 1d6, and they double the critical threat range of any light weapon they wield when attacking a target that is flanked or denied its Dexterity bonus. This does not stack with the Improved Critical feat, keen edge, and similar effects.

Supreme Stealth (Ex)

At 10th level, a master thief can use the skill unlocks for Stealth as though they had 5 more ranks in that skill than they actually possess and can make Stealth checks even when directly observed..
